mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the next 20 days signals an easing monetary cycle, compressing discount rates and boosting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window, or 20-day returns in easing periods not significantly higher than baseline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A surge in labor employment (PAYEMS) above 1.5 million persons triggers positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days, reflecting strong labor market confidence and growth expectations.
failure_condition: 20-day returns not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) despite PAYEMS exceeding threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in monthly demand (RSAFS) and demand units (HOUST) above their 50th percentile triggers positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days, signaling robust economic activity.
candidate_trigger: both RSAFS and HOUST exceed 50th percentile in the same month
failure_condition: Interaction effect not statistically significant (IC < 0.05) or returns not positive when proxies rise.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS >5.0%), a sustained increase in FEDFUNDS over 20 days predicts negative S&P 500 returns due to higher borrowing costs.
failure_condition: 20-day returns not significantly negative (p >0.05) during tightening periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the supply index (INDPRO) over 60 days signals robust production capacity, driving positive S&P 500 returns through stronger economic fundamentals.
failure_condition: 60-day returns not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p >0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% triggers positive S&P 500 returns within 5 days, reflecting strong labor market health and growth prospects.
failure_condition: 5-day returns not significantly positive (p >0.05) despite UNRATE crossing below threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS <5.0%) and rising quarterly demand (GDPC1) over 20 days predicts positive S&P 500 returns through easing financing costs and demand expansion.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS <5.0% and GDPC1 rises >2% in the same month
failure_condition: Interaction effect not significant (IC <0.05) or returns not positive when both proxies rise.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle demand expansion (GDPC1 growth between 1% and 2%), sustained 60-day S&P 500 returns remain positive as growth expectations persist despite slowing momentum.
failure_condition: 60-day returns not significantly positive (p >0.05) during late-cycle growth.
